minutes.headline: COA voted to formally oppose turning Memorial Drive into green space, citing parking and safety impacts.
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging reviewed FY26 budget changes that shifted two KitchenAide positions and the meal site manager into the town budget while losing a part-time outreach coordinator, heard a presentation from an outgoing assessor on senior tax deferral and circuit-breaker programs, and discussed FY27 staffing priorities including a new program coordinator and a title change to assistant director. The board voted to oppose converting Memorial Drive into a permanent green space and heard updates on the kitchen renovation, an elevator/space study for August's capital plan, the 300th anniversary bonfire, and Eagle House Supporters fundraising.

votes.motion: That the Council on Aging is not in favor of making Memorial Drive a green space, due to the impact on the senior center and teen center parking

budget_items.topic: Kiosk sign funded by CPA/'opa' funds
budget_items.what_was_said: A board member noted the outdoor kiosk was purchased with community funds and proposed repurposing its panels into three large readable posters rather than abandoning it.

The town's FY26 senior center budget was reported to lose a part-time outreach coordinator; the director clarified the two KitchenAide positions moved from a grant into the town budget and the meal site manager position moved from part-time to full-time.
The senior center's programs budget was said to have increased, described elsewhere as roughly a 30% increase.
Town meeting approved funding for a parking lot study as part of flooring and parking lot capital plans.

budget_items.topic: Circuit breaker and tax deferral program
budget_items.what_was_said: The outgoing assessor described the state circuit breaker rebate and a new senior tax deferral program, including income eligibility and monthly savings.

budget_items.topic: FY27 budget request: program coordinator and title change
budget_items.what_was_said: For FY27 the director proposed a new program coordinator position and a title change from outreach coordinator to assistant director/outreach, as the top staffing priorities.
The director suggested adding a dedicated meal budget line to buffer costs, since seniors currently pay a flat per-meal price that does not always cover costs.
An elevator/Lula lift study for the old section of the building will need to go into the August capital plan through facilities.
A July senior trip to Gloucester for a harbor cruise and lobster buffet was announced with a per-person cost.

budget_items.topic: Parking lot study cited again re: green space debate
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair noted the town already budgeted a parking lot study for next year, used as an argument against converting the drive to green space.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to repurpose the existing kiosk into three large posters (Eagle House info, COA info, weekly program schedule); one member volunteered to lead design and printing and offered to fund it.
Board agreed to look into an AI-assisted minutes-taking tool used by another town committee (storm water) to ease the minutes burden.
Chair/staff agreed to email the agenda to all board members going forward once it is posted to the town.
Board informally nominated Deb and Jane to continue as officers for FY26, with the slate to come to a formal vote at the next meeting.
Board agreed to hold its usual end-of-fiscal-year party at the last meeting of the year, with Elena coordinating sign-ups for food.
Kathy was named the board's new liaison to the Eagle House Supporters, replacing Elena.
A board member agreed to draft a request to local garden centers asking for donated plants for the pavilion area.
A board member volunteered to help Pauline develop a senior healthcare advisory/resource group, drawing on her own caregiving and medical-records experience.

what_happened.line: The board voted to oppose converting Memorial Drive into a permanent green space, citing parking and safety at the senior and teen centers.
FY26 moved two KitchenAide positions and the meal site manager into the town budget while a part-time outreach coordinator position was lost.
For FY27 the director will request a new program coordinator and a title change from outreach coordinator to assistant director.
An elevator/accessibility study for the building's older section is set to go into the town's August capital plan.

why_it_matters: The Memorial Drive vote is a position the board is putting on record ahead of any town decision on the parcel's use.
Moving positions from grant to town funding, and losing others, changes what the senior center budget line covers going forward.
The FY27 staffing requests and the capital-plan elevator study are items that will come before the town for funding.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the main decisions (Memorial Drive vote, kiosk posters, officer nomination, end-of-year party, new Supporters liaison, donated plants), differing mostly in wording and in which names the captions got wrong. The thing to know is that the official minutes record a vote approving the prior minutes that ours omit, and that ours misassigns roles (Pauline as director, Caesar as board member) and carries budget figures the official minutes do not give.
